player_action: I want to ready an action with the trigger 'when anything bad happens'.
correct_ruling: A readied action needs a specified condition and action; whether a vague trigger like 'anything bad' is acceptable is up to the DM, who should ask for a concrete trigger.
common_wrong_rulings: Accepts an omni-trigger that fires whenever convenient.

player_action: We're in a tavern brawl, nobody's drawn steel yet. Do we roll initiative now, when I start shouting?
correct_ruling: The SRD says initiative is rolled when combat starts; exactly when a tense scene becomes combat is the DM's call.

player_action: Can I open the door, step through, and close it behind me all as one move?
correct_ruling: Opening or closing a door is a move action in the SRD action table; combining both with movement in one action isn't specified, so the DM rules on it (by RAW it's likely two move actions plus movement, i.e., the whole round).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Actions in Combat table > Open or close a door
confidence_note: Open/close door listed as move action in the SRD table; combination ruling is DM judgment.

player_action: I want to use Spot to notice the hidden archer in the middle of my turn — what action is that?
correct_ruling: Spot is typically a reactive check made when there's a chance to notice something (no action); actively trying to spot is a move action. The DM decides when reactive checks are called for.

player_action: Since I delayed last round and never acted, I want to take two turns this round to catch up.
game_state: Rogue delayed through an entire round without acting.
correct_ruling: If you delay past a full round you simply lose that round's actions; you never get two turns. The rogue acts once and its initiative is set where it acts.

player_action: I'm fast, I have Improved Initiative and a 20 Dex, so I should get to act in the surprise round even though I failed my Spot check.
game_state: Fighter unaware of the ambush (failed Spot).
correct_ruling: Only characters aware of opponents act in the surprise round. Initiative modifiers don't make you aware; the fighter is flat-footed and doesn't act in the surprise round.

player_action: I take the Dodge action and then use Disengage.
correct_ruling: There are no Dodge or Disengage actions in 3.5 (those are 5e). The closest are fighting defensively or total defense for AC, and withdraw (full-round) or a 5-foot step to leave without provoking.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Total Defense; Fighting Defensively; Withdraw

correct_ruling: Total defense is a standard action giving +4 dodge bonus to AC for 1 round; you can't attack (or make AoOs) and can still move. (5 or more Tumble ranks raise the bonus to +6.)
